title: A solar-velocity absorption term cuts HD 69830 full CCF squared residuals by 97.5 percent in six HARPS exposures
abstract: We test a solar blend explanation for the selected HD 69830 twilight velocity excursion of 2019 November 6. We retrieve one event and five dark reference CCFs from ESO. A first-order Sun-observer velocity of -0.815 km/s changes the expected blue separation from 4.625 to 5.439 km/s. This resolves the main gap with a prior 5.429 km/s Gaussian fit. Adding absorption at the predicted center cuts full CCF squared residuals by 97.5 percent compared with a shifted and widened empirical stellar profile. Nine window and continuum choices give 96.3-98.9 percent reductions. Separate blue and red order groups also show the effect. The fixed-model event residual is near the dark-reference control scale. But free centers differ between order groups and depend on model choices. The calculation omits solar line zero points and uses a Gaussian contaminant. No solar template, sky spectrum or independent instrument confirms the cause. We find no new planet. Code, input URLs and hashes, aggregate results, figures and replay steps are included. Original ESO files stay in shared storage.

display.caption: Event minus fitted profile in three CCF groups. Base: shifted and widened empirical reference. Fixed: extra absorption at the first-order solar velocity. Free: extra absorption with a free center. Credit: ESO; new analysis of DRS 3.8 products, DOI 10.18727/archive/33.

Adding the Sun-observer radial term resolves the main gap with the earlier two-Gaussian separation. Full-profile free-center fits remain model dependent. ESO source data; prior model from SCI 8cab0ef9.
